workflow: demo login UI and synthetic local browser regression

checks: five named accounts are visible left of the desktop form and fill the selected phone
code and copy icon write the real clipboard and show local confirmation without submitting
choosing another account clears the previous challenge and copy confirmation
keyboard activation copies the code and clipboard denial uses a working fallback
copy failure is explicit and does not claim success or submit login
all accounts stay expanded and layouts fit 320, 390, 768 and 1440 pixels
selected doctor can complete the unchanged OTP login and reach their role
loginBrowser.clipboard: real Chromium clipboard; denied API fallback; both methods denied

checks.counting: 24 individual browser checks; 27 including three parent wrappers

baseline.scope: 78 individual API/calendar/UX/roles/edge/presentation/startup checks. These are historical baseline results, not rerun totals for 1.9.

features: Five named sample accounts always expanded to the left of desktop login; compact mobile account grid
Selecting a sample fills phone, focuses its field and clears previous challenge and code
OTP value and adjacent icon both copy with local success tooltip; keyboard support and truthful clipboard failure
Same-account session reauthentication retains answers and does not offer account switching
limitations: Real Android/iPhone camera and GPS not tested
Home visits remain demo-only; production provider/retention agreements not implemented
City starter catalog is not a nationwide official dataset
Public site uses browser-local storage; no shared cross-device patient database
SMS, banking, provider appointment confirmation and live medical operation remain unconnected
Startup improvement verified with controlled delays, not measured on user network
Safari and Firefox not tested; no comprehensive security/load audit or clinical validation

publicBrowser.reason: Chromium does not trust the environment proxy CA; automatic approval review rejected a persistent trust-store addition. TLS verification was not disabled. Public HTTPS byte comparison succeeded; browser behavior was tested locally.
